name: Unnao–Gazole Highway
aka: Formed from stretches of the old NH 232A, NH 231, NH 56, NH 29, NH 19, NH 30, NH 31 and NH 81
history: NH 31 links central Uttar Pradesh with northern West Bengal, staying close to the river Ganga for much of the way. It was created after the 2010 renumbering by joining several older highways into one route, including the old Ghazipur–Patna road that was once NH 19. The highway crosses the Ganga twice, at Patna and near Mokama, before ending at Kodubari Morh near Gazole in Malda district, where it meets NH 12.
facts: About 990 km long, from Unnao in Uttar Pradesh to Gazole in West Bengal.
Crosses the Ganga twice — on the 5.7 km Mahatma Gandhi Setu between Hajipur and Patna, and on the Rajendra Setu near Mokama.
Passes through the holy city of Varanasi and the ancient city of Patna.
A different road from the famous old NH 31 to Assam — most of that older route is now numbered NH 27.
